title: The Cell System: a coordinate system for the odd sieve — what it proves, what it measures, and where it stops
description:
Seven documents on the elementary sieve of the odd numbers, developed as a coordinate system of lines and cells.

Papers 0–IV build the construction and prove what it decides. Paper V derives the point at which it stops from inside the construction rather than quoting it: the framework reproduces Buchstab's decomposition, the Hardy–Littlewood singular series and the exact factor-of-two loss I(s) = 2f1(s) without importing them, and then halts exactly where the field halts. (The sifting limits are quoted from the literature, not derived here.) It measures how much of the difficulty can be localised first — to a set of density 10-3 — and shows that the quantity a weighted sieve argument evaluates transfers from cycle to window with a relative error of 0.36%, so the computation is not the obstruction. Paper 0 is independent of the rest and concerns no prime numbers: an exact five-term histogram for the increments of floor(2j²/n), with no error term.

Statements that are only measured are labelled as such and listed together; results produced and then retracted during the work are kept rather than deleted. No progress toward the twin-prime conjecture is claimed, and no new bound. Priority is not claimed for any result.

This release restructures the two largest papers so that each is read in the order its content warrants. Paper IV now runs gap alphabet → twin criterion → clocks and originality → inheritance across sectors → prime-gate belts → named tracks, with the distance-6 closing budget — whose object is a prime pair (p, p+6) rather than a twin pair — moved to an appendix so that it no longer interrupts that line. Paper V states the obstruction first: the depth cut, the unique-owner theorem, the exact twin count T = C − R + S and the parity identity 2(R − C) = Σ(−1)Ω, then why no ordinary sieve crosses it, and only then the routes that were tried before the identity was written, each arriving at the same place. Fifteen stale or incorrect cross-references were corrected in the process; Paper IV was given its own reference list, having previously cited external works through Paper V's numbering; every reference in every paper is now cited in that paper's own body; and the standing disclaimer now appears in Papers I, II and III as well, so that a reader who downloads one paper alone sees it.

Seven verification scripts regenerate every number printed, each exiting non-zero when the claim it supports fails.
